newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium advances, revived by LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium advances, revived by LME gains.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures closed higher across the board on Wednesday, with buying by trade houses more than offsetting profit-taking by individual speculators, traders said.
"Now that the LME has started to move up again, this market might be revived," said one trader at a major trading house.
"Everybody must be happy today. Individual traders took profits, and we sold as there was a price difference of about $10 (with London) at the beginning," he added.

TOCOM aluminium ended 3.5 to 2.7 yen higher, with the benchmark February 1998 contract up 2.7 yen at 207.5 yen per kg. The day's volume, while thin at 5,792 lots, was the second largest after 19,645 lots on April 7 when the contract was launched.
"The Tokyo aluminium market might change when the next contract is introduced on April 25," said another trader.
